hook.line: At the neighbourhood meeting, Don Hernando wants everyone to hear his view before the shouting starts. Spanish has a few ready-made ways to say what you think.
hook.es: En mi opinión, el transporte público es caro.
hook.en: In my opinion, public transport is expensive.

examples.es: A mí me parece que el barrio está más seguro.
examples.en: I think the neighbourhood is safer.

examples.es: En mi opinión, el transporte público es caro.
examples.en: In my opinion, public transport is expensive.

examples.es: Desde mi punto de vista, la basura es el problema.
examples.en: From my point of view, the rubbish is the problem.

examples.es: A Hernando le parece que la alcaldía no hace nada.
examples.en: Hernando thinks the council does nothing.
In your opinion, who's right? (to a friend)

examples.en: From our point of view, the price is high.

rule:
Three ready-made starters:
*En mi opinión,* *Desde mi punto de vista,* and *A mí me parece que*.

After the first two, put a comma and then a normal sentence. After *me parece que*, no comma.

Swap *mi* for *tu*, *su*, *nuestro*, or swap *a mí me* for *a ti te*, *a Hernando le*, *a nosotros nos*.

When you are stating your view positively, the verb after is the normal one: *es caro*, *está seguro*. The wish form shows up only when you say you *don't* think so.

*Me parece que* is everyday speech. *Desde mi punto de vista* sounds more measured.
smallPrint: Teachers call these opinion markers (*marcadores de opinión*).

options: I think the council does nothing.
Hernando thinks the council does nothing.
Hernando thinks I do nothing.

options: In your opinion, public transport is expensive.
In my opinion, public transport is expensive.
In his opinion, public transport is expensive.
In your opinion, who's right? (to a friend)

readAndPick.es: A mí me parece que el barrio está más seguro.
options: Hernando thinks the neighbourhood is safer.
I think the neighbourhood is safer.
You think the neighbourhood is safer.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: In my opinion, public transport is expensive.
yourTurn.answer: En mi opinión, el transporte público es caro.
yourTurn.why: *En mi opinión* is followed by a comma and a normal sentence.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: From my point of view, the rubbish is the problem.
yourTurn.answer: Desde mi punto de vista, la basura es el problema.
yourTurn.why: *Desde mi punto de vista* works the same way, with *mi* for you.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I think the neighbourhood is safer.
yourTurn.answer: A mí me parece que el barrio está más seguro.
accept: Me parece que el barrio está más seguro.
yourTurn.why: *Me parece que* needs no comma, and the verb after it is the normal one.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Hernando thinks the council does nothing.
yourTurn.answer: A Hernando le parece que la alcaldía no hace nada.
yourTurn.why: Swap *a mí me* for *a Hernando le*.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: In your opinion, who's right?
Make it about us: *A mí me parece que la calle es peligrosa.*
yourTurn.answer: A nosotros nos parece que la calle es peligrosa.
yourTurn.why: *A mí me* becomes *a nosotros nos*, and *parece* stays.

yourTurn.prompt: Change *En mi opinión* to *Desde mi punto de vista*: *En mi opinión, hay mucha basura.*
yourTurn.answer: Desde mi punto de vista, hay mucha basura.
yourTurn.why: The two starters are interchangeable, and the rest of the sentence stays.

pitfalls.wrong: Para mi opinión, el precio es alto.
pitfalls.right: En mi opinión, el precio es alto.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Spanish says *in* my opinion too: *en mi opinión*.

pitfalls.wrong: En mi opinión que el precio es alto.
pitfalls.right: En mi opinión, el precio es alto.
pitfalls.why: Almost. No *que* after *en mi opinión*: just a comma and the sentence.
When you state your view positively, the verb is the normal one: *es*.

personal: Give your view on something in your own street, once with *En mi opinión,* and once with *A mí me parece que*.
